item.content:encoded:
Awesome blend between comedy and serious "realism" in the mechanics of the rating system. The only source of confusion for me was the way a positive rating is determined. At the beginning of the info sheet, it refers to ratings being based off of the evaluations of observers. Does this mean stated, thought-out evaluations, or just the general reaction one feels? If the latter, how does the Ratings Committee exert complete influence over the ratings? In that case, every observer, not just the Ratings Committee members, would have an effect on the rating of an object. Also, I love how meta this is. Upvoted!

TL;DR - How an object's rating is determined based off of observers is a bit confusing (to me at least) and could be explained more effectively.

item.content:encoded:
This tale was originally posted in Chinese on CN Branch as the champion entry of the Parallel World's Foundation Tales Contest.

Translated -> Posted on EN Site -> Downvoted by people -> Rewritten by Dr Cimmerian -> Reposted here.

Another translated version can be found on the International Translation Archive (scp-int), translated by CN Branch staff. Readers may compare differences between original and rewritten versions.

"Are we gods?" T.D. moved the food on his plate around into various shapes.

"Sure." The supervisor nodded his head. "And we're the good guys."

This was some funny shit. I don't see why some people are wrinkling their noses at the concept, because it's obviously not promoting itself as canon - more as a jokey, unserious explanation for the immersion-wrecking little box at the top of every mainlister, and the way a fantastical and dangerous creature can appear in our html universe and then be wiped from existence in under 48 hours, because it was a giant telepathic Fifthist werewolf with red eyes and diamond claws that eats people (but only in multiples of five because Fifthism) and the Foundation thought it was really generic.

Normally we just ignore this stuff in-universe, because any explanation would unavoidably end up sounding really, really silly - but I'm glad someone went and tried to explain it anyway.

item.content:encoded:
I'm not sure I understand the enthusiasm for the concept behind this tale. It makes precious little sense - I know that is kind of the point, but I prefer my meta with at least some viability in-universe. Here, the Foundation are "gods" that can determine the continued existence of anomalies, but they somehow don't control the standards. So can they choose to downvote, or are their choices predetermined?

Either way, all of the tension of the setting is destroyed. Under one option, the Foundation is in total control of anomalies and is in no real danger. Under the other, the Foundation's ability to influence the "rating system" is illusory, so it may as well not exist (not to mention that it kills off tension through predestination).

Wrapping that unsatisfactory concept in a goofy tone does nothing for me, I'm afraid.
